true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The new downsize definition replaces the width/height API

Ruby does not overload methods by argument signature, so this second definition replaces the existing downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) method. Calls using four arguments now treat max_height as the options hash and fail when optimize accesses opts[:allow_animation]; calls supplying a fifth options argument fail with ArgumentError. Preserve the previously supported width/height form in a single compatible implementation.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Do not impose the image input ceiling on attachments

This hard-coded 10 MiB limit applies to attachments as well as images, replacing the configured max_attachment_size_kb limit even though attachments are not downsized. A site configured to permit attachments larger than 10 MiB now has otherwise-valid uploads rejected by the browser before they reach the server. Retain the configured attachment limit and apply the preprocessing ceiling only to images.

true_positives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Percentage geometry is unsupported by the animated GIF resizer

When allow_animated_thumbnails is enabled and the GIF tempfile has a .gif extension, downsize selects the animated implementation, which emits gifsicle --resize-fit 80%. That option requires width/height geometry rather than a percentage, so all five attempts fail and the oversized animated GIF remains above the upload limit. Use a GIF scaling operation or calculate explicit target dimensions.

true_positives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Reopen the tempfile after in-place optimization

OptimizedImage.downsize calls ImageOptim.optimize_image!, which can replace the file at its pathname with an optimized file. The already-open tempfile then still references the old inode. Subsequent tempfile.size checks can remain stuck at an earlier size, and the filesize passed to Upload.create_for can differ from the resized file on disk. This can reject an image that was successfully reduced below the limit or record an incorrect filesize. Reopen the resulting file before checking its size and creating the upload, or resize into a separate tempfile.

true_positives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Guard missing hosts before string normalization

The before_validation callback calls sub! on host without checking for nil. Creating or updating through the new endpoint with an omitted or null host therefore raises NoMethodError instead of returning the validation errors handled by save_host. The same exception occurs when validating EmbeddableHost.new. Guard normalization and validate the required host so malformed input produces a controlled error response.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Normalize legacy hosts during migration

The old host-matching logic supported entries containing schemes and paths, such as https://example.com/1234. This INSERT copies those entries verbatim and bypasses EmbeddableHost's normalization callback. The new lookup compares the stored value with URI.host, so these migrated entries never match example.com. Existing embedded comments consequently return access errors and topic retrieval stops after upgrading. Normalize each legacy entry before inserting it.

true_positives.golden_comment: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Quote host values instead of interpolating them into SQL

Each legacy host value is interpolated directly into a single-quoted SQL literal. A URL containing an apostrophe in its path, such as https://example.com/it's, breaks the INSERT and aborts the upgrade; crafted values can also alter the SQL statement. Use bound values or connection.quote rather than treating persisted setting text as SQL.

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Handle an unset embed category before indexing the query result

The category query returns no rows when embed_category was never configured or names a deleted or renamed category. Indexing its result with [0]['id'] then raises before reaching the uncategorized fallback. This prevents db:migrate from completing on installations that do not use embedding, including clean databases. Read the optional result safely and also handle a missing uncategorized_category_id setting.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

false_positives.candidate:
Allow valid hostnames with longer top-level domains

The hostname regex limits the final suffix to two through five letters, rejecting valid domains such as example.museum and example.technology. Administrators cannot add these hosts. Legacy entries inserted by the migration bypass validation, but subsequently changing their category also fails validation. Hostname validation should not impose this obsolete TLD-length restriction.

Enforce one category mapping per normalized hostname

Neither the model nor the table prevents duplicate hostnames, including case variants. Administrators can save example.com twice with different categories, but record_for_host always selects the first matching row. Editing the other row succeeds without changing the category used for imports, leaving a configuration that the application silently ignores. Enforce case-insensitive hostname uniqueness in validation and the database.

Make port-qualified host storage and lookup consistent

Validation accepts example.com:8080, and normalization retains the port, including when an administrator enters https://example.com:8080. However, URI.host returns only example.com, which can never match the stored example.com:8080 value. A successfully saved port-qualified host therefore cannot embed comments or retrieve topics. Normalize storage and lookup consistently, or reject port-qualified entries explicitly.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Handle an absent TopicUser record

TopicUser.find_by can return nil: for example, a forwarded notification for a public topic can be opened by another logged-in account that has never visited that topic. Access to the topic does not guarantee a topic-user row exists. Dereferencing tu.notification_level then raises NoMethodError and returns a server error instead of unsubscribing. Treat the missing row as the default notification level and create the preference through TopicUser.change.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
Do not change notification preferences through an unprotected GET

This GET invokes TopicsController#unsubscribe, which immediately saves a new notification level for the logged-in user. The URL is predictable, has no unsubscribe token, and bypasses check_xhr; Rails' normal CSRF protection does not validate GET requests. An attacker can therefore send a logged-in victim through a cross-site navigation to silence notifications for an accessible topic. Make GET display a confirmation and perform the change through a CSRF-protected POST.

Do not promise that Regular disables all topic notifications

The confirmation says the user will stop receiving notifications for the topic, but the controller changes Watching or Tracking users to Regular rather than Muted. Regular still allows notifications and notification emails for mentions and replies to the user, so the confirmation promises more than the operation provides. Describe the notifications that remain enabled, or change the operation to match the promise.

Keep the topic URL optional in the shared unsubscribe footer

The shared unsubscribe_link translation now unconditionally requires unsubscribe_url, but Email::MessageBuilder still accepts add_unsubscribe_link without supplying that value. A previously supported call such as MessageBuilder.new(address, body: "hello", add_unsubscribe_link: true).body now raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument instead of building an email. Both text and HTML footer generation use this translation. Preserve the generic preferences-only footer and add the topic paragraph only when a topic unsubscribe URL is available.

Mark unsubscription as an explicit notification preference change

Saving notification_level directly bypasses the bookkeeping in TopicUser.change, particularly setting notifications_reason_id to user_changed. For an existing topic-user row whose reason is NULL, an unsubscribe can set the level to Muted but leave it eligible for automatic tracking. TopicUser.update_last_read then changes it back to Tracking once the reading-time threshold is met, undoing the mute and re-enabling notifications. Use the normal notification-change helper so the explicit preference is preserved.

Persist the unsubscribe change during client-side navigation

This route only loads the ordinary topic view; it never invokes the unsubscribe endpoint or changes the notification level. If an already-loaded Discourse application navigates to the unsubscribe URL client-side, the initial HTML request to TopicsController#unsubscribe never happens. The page nevertheless tells the user notifications will stop, while their subscription remains unchanged. The client-side flow needs to perform the subscription change explicitly.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Concurrent matches lose counter increments

The read-modify-save sequence is not atomic. Two requests matching the same address can both read match_count as N and both save N+1, recording only one of the two matches. Concurrent registration attempts therefore undercount blocked-email activity. Increment the counter atomically in the database or protect the update with a row lock.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Case-sensitive matching allows blocked addresses to bypass the ban

Neither BlockedEmail creation nor this lookup normalizes the address. A block for `bad@spammers.org` therefore does not match `bad@SPAMMERS.ORG`, even though email domains are case-insensitive. A user can change the domain's capitalization to pass the new validation and register with the same blocked mailbox. Apply consistent email normalization when storing and looking up blocked addresses.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

false_positives.candidate:
Rejected user saves roll back the match statistics

When this helper runs inside User.save or User.save!, the BlockedEmail save joins the enclosing user transaction. The email validator then adds a blocking error, causing Rails to roll back that transaction—including match_count and last_match_at. Paths such as User.create_for_email, which calls save! without a preceding standalone valid? call, reject the address without recording the match. Persist rejected-match statistics independently of the failed user transaction and cover this through a user-save integration test.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Preserve HTML sanitization for raw-HTML posts

Returning `raw` bypasses sanitization as well as Markdown rendering. RSS bodies reach this path after only entity decoding and a Nokogiri parse, which preserve scripts and event handlers. The importer also interpolates the attribution URL directly into HTML, so a valid article URL containing `?x='onmouseover='alert(1)` can inject an event-handler attribute even when Readability cleaned the article. This output is persisted as cooked HTML and rendered unescaped on the forum origin. Imported posts also retain this unsafe cooking mode on subsequent edits.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Fix the invalid closing conditional in the embed template

The template closes its conditional with `end if`, but the trailing `if` has no condition. ERB therefore generates invalid Ruby and raises a syntax error when rendering this view. Once an embedded topic has been retrieved, requests switch from the loading page to a server error instead of displaying the discussion.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Handle standard RSS body fields and entries without content

Valid RSS feeds commonly put article HTML in `description` or `content:encoded`, while Atom entries may provide only `summary`. These entries do not have an `i.content` value, so calling `scrub` on it fails and aborts the entire polling run before subsequent entries are imported. Select an available body field and explicitly handle entries with no body.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

false_positives.candidate:
Bound remotely downloaded content before parsing it

The visitor-controlled embed URL is restricted only by host, so it can identify a large video, archive, or other asset on the allowed site rather than an article. `open(url).read` downloads and buffers the complete response, then passes it to Readability/Nokogiri without a size limit or content-type check. Such requests can exhaust the Sidekiq process's memory. Enforce a download-size limit and reject unsuitable responses before HTML parsing.

Defer post-processing jobs until the outer import transaction commits

PostCreator.create enqueues feature_topic_users and process_post after its own transaction block, but this caller wraps that block in an outer Topic.transaction. The nested transaction has not committed when those jobs are published, so separate Sidekiq workers can run before the post or topic is visible. If creating the embed subsequently fails, the jobs reference rolled-back records. Job publication needs to occur after the outermost transaction commits.

Do not require archived Disqus source pages to remain reachable

Importing each thread now performs a remote page fetch without exception handling. A normal 404 or connection failure for an archived permalink raises from open-uri and aborts the entire import, even though that thread's comments and all subsequent threads are already available in the XML export. Retain a permalink-only fallback when retrieving the source article fails so the comment migration can still complete.

Handle simultaneous imports of the same URL

The existence lookup occurs before the creation transaction and does not serialize imports. The hourly feed poll and on-demand retrievals can import the same feed concurrently, allowing both callers to observe no embed and create a topic before one loses the unique embed_url insert race. The resulting RecordNotUnique exception aborts that feed's remaining entries, and scheduled polling has retries disabled. Serialize creation per URL or recover from the conflict by loading the winning embed.

Preserve original thread timestamps during Disqus imports

The old topic creation forwarded the Disqus thread's created_at value, but import_remote receives only its title and creates the initial post with the current time. Replies still retain their historical dates. Imported discussions therefore have a first post newer than their replies and are dated and ordered as newly created discussions rather than preserving the exported history. Forward the thread timestamp through the import helpers.

Resolve relative URLs using URI semantics

The current rewriting turns a protocol-relative URL such as `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` into `http://article-host/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`, losing the intended host. It also leaves path-relative values such as `images/photo.jpg` unchanged, so they resolve against the Discourse page instead of the source article. This breaks common imported links and images. Resolve both href and src values against the article URL rather than stripping leading slashes and concatenating a host prefix.

Set the retrieval throttle and its expiration atomically

SETNX creates the throttle key without an expiration, and EXPIRE is issued separately. If EXPIRE fails or the worker exits between these commands, the article has not been retrieved but its key remains permanently present. Every later retrieval then reports it as recently retrieved, leaving the embed on the loading page indefinitely. Set the key and its TTL in one atomic operation.

Update dependency locks for the other supported Rails boot modes

The new dependencies are unconditional, but only Gemfile_rails4.lock is updated. This Gemfile still selects Gemfile.lock in RAILS3 mode and Gemfile_rails_master.lock in RAILS_MASTER mode. Frozen or deployment installs using those modes now have lockfiles that disagree with the Gemfile and fail dependency installation. Update the corresponding lockfiles or scope the dependencies to the supported mode.

Validate redirect destinations during embedded-page retrieval

TopicRetriever checks the allowlisted host only on the original embed URL, but `open(url)` follows HTTP redirects without rechecking their destinations. An allowed-host URL that redirects elsewhere can therefore make the worker fetch off-allowlist or internal services, potentially importing their responses into a topic. The embed-triggered retrieval path must enforce its host restriction before following each redirect.

true_positives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Preserve panel positioning in the legacy flexbox fallback

Browsers using the newly emitted `display: -webkit-box` fallback, such as the Android 4.3 stock browser, do not distribute remaining space through auto margins in that box model. With `float: right` removed and no preceding item assigned `-webkit-box-flex: 1`, the header panel is packed immediately after the logo/topic information rather than against the right edge. The legacy fallback needs a flexible preceding item or another compatible right-alignment mechanism.

false_negatives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

false_positives.candidate:
Include alignment for the Mozilla box fallback

The display mixins emit `-moz-box` and `-moz-inline-box`, but the alignment mixin omits `-moz-box-align`. Firefox versions using those legacy display values ignore all the emitted alignment properties and retain the default stretch alignment. In particular, switching bullet badges from their inline-block fallback to `-moz-inline-box` now loses the intended baseline alignment between the category marker and its text. Emit the matching Mozilla alignment property.

Preserve right-aligned controls in the small-action flex layout

The new flex layout leaves `.small-action-desc` content-sized because it has no positive flex-grow, while action buttons still rely on `float: right`. That float cannot preserve right-edge placement: it is ignored on direct flex children, and buttons inside the description can only float to the edge of its now-narrow box. Short action notices therefore pull their controls next to the notice instead of keeping them at the row's right edge. Make the description consume the remaining space and use flex-aware positioning for the controls.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Apply the website visibility restriction to website_name

Unlike `website`, `website_name` is not covered by `untrusted_attributes`, so it bypasses `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`. For a TL0 user viewed anonymously, the serializer now exposes the hidden website's host and potentially its path, and the updated template displays that information even though `website` is omitted. The `include_website_name` method is also not a recognized inclusion predicate because it lacks the trailing `?`; correcting that alone would still leave the trust restriction bypassed. Apply the same visibility guard used for `website`.

false_positives.candidate:
Do not identify shared domains by removing the first DNS label

Comparing everything after the first label treats unrelated domains under multi-label public suffixes as the same domain. For example, an instance at `example.co.uk` and a website at `https://other.co.uk/user` both have three labels and both reduce to `co.uk`, so this branch incorrectly displays the full path for an unrelated website. Use a registrable-domain-aware comparison, or restrict matching to explicitly supported host relationships, rather than assuming the first label is always a subdomain.

Keep website_name synchronized when the website changes

The label now uses a value fetched from the server rather than a computed property dependent on `model.website`. When the loaded user model's website is edited and saved, `User.save()` only copies `bio_excerpt` from the response and never refreshes `website_name`. Consequently, the existing profile header can display the old host/path while its link points to the new website, or continue hiding the website if it was initially empty. Update the derived value after saving or retain a client-side computation that follows website changes.

true_positives.golden_comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Restore the 30%/70% shades for embedded-post author links

The original author-link color used 30% lightness, but this replacement uses 70% for light themes and 30% for dark themes. Both branches now give these small author links the much dimmer shade: a black/white palette produces #b3b3b3 on white or #4d4d4d on black, with only about 2:1–2.5:1 contrast. Preserve 30% in the light branch and use 70% in the dark branch, as the regular post-author links do.

true_positives.golden_comment: This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Keep group-member names at their original contrast level

The group-member name previously used 30% lightness, but the new light branch uses 50%. The same change appears in app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss at line 497. This unnecessarily reduces the contrast of normal-size member names in light themes: with a #222 primary and white secondary, it changes approximately #646464 to #919191, dropping contrast from about 5.9:1 to 3.2:1. Preserve the 30% light-theme value and use 70% for its dark-theme counterpart instead of copying the title's 50% shade.

true_positives.golden_comment: The light theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, which may unintentionally reduce contrast and affect readability. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with design intentions.
