The newly introduced ContextualLoggerMiddleware does not add this information, resulting in missing traceID in plugin request logs and impacting debugging and request tracing capabilities.

true_positives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Guard missing hosts before string normalization

The before_validation callback calls sub! on host without checking for nil. Creating or updating through the new endpoint with an omitted or null host therefore raises NoMethodError instead of returning the validation errors handled by save_host. The same exception occurs when validating EmbeddableHost.new. Guard normalization and validate the required host so malformed input produces a controlled error response.

false_positives.candidate:
Validate redirect destinations during embedded-page retrieval

TopicRetriever checks the allowlisted host only on the original embed URL, but `open(url)` follows HTTP redirects without rechecking their destinations. An allowed-host URL that redirects elsewhere can therefore make the worker fetch off-allowlist or internal services, potentially importing their responses into a topic. The embed-triggered retrieval path must enforce its host restriction before following each redirect.

Bound remotely downloaded content before parsing it

The visitor-controlled embed URL is restricted only by host, so it can identify a large video, archive, or other asset on the allowed site rather than an article. `open(url).read` downloads and buffers the complete response, then passes it to Readability/Nokogiri without a size limit or content-type check. Such requests can exhaust the Sidekiq process's memory. Enforce a download-size limit and reject unsuitable responses before HTML parsing.

Resolve relative URLs using URI semantics

The current rewriting turns a protocol-relative URL such as `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` into `http://article-host/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`, losing the intended host. It also leaves path-relative values such as `images/photo.jpg` unchanged, so they resolve against the Discourse page instead of the source article. This breaks common imported links and images. Resolve both href and src values against the article URL rather than stripping leading slashes and concatenating a host prefix.

Defer post-processing jobs until the outer import transaction commits

PostCreator.create enqueues feature_topic_users and process_post after its own transaction block, but this caller wraps that block in an outer Topic.transaction. The nested transaction has not committed when those jobs are published, so separate Sidekiq workers can run before the post or topic is visible. If creating the embed subsequently fails, the jobs reference rolled-back records. Job publication needs to occur after the outermost transaction commits.

Handle simultaneous imports of the same URL

The existence lookup occurs before the creation transaction and does not serialize imports. The hourly feed poll and on-demand retrievals can import the same feed concurrently, allowing both callers to observe no embed and create a topic before one loses the unique embed_url insert race. The resulting RecordNotUnique exception aborts that feed's remaining entries, and scheduled polling has retries disabled. Serialize creation per URL or recover from the conflict by loading the winning embed.

Set the retrieval throttle and its expiration atomically

SETNX creates the throttle key without an expiration, and EXPIRE is issued separately. If EXPIRE fails or the worker exits between these commands, the article has not been retrieved but its key remains permanently present. Every later retrieval then reports it as recently retrieved, leaving the embed on the loading page indefinitely. Set the key and its TTL in one atomic operation.

Preserve original thread timestamps during Disqus imports

The old topic creation forwarded the Disqus thread's created_at value, but import_remote receives only its title and creates the initial post with the current time. Replies still retain their historical dates. Imported discussions therefore have a first post newer than their replies and are dated and ordered as newly created discussions rather than preserving the exported history. Forward the thread timestamp through the import helpers.

Do not require archived Disqus source pages to remain reachable

Importing each thread now performs a remote page fetch without exception handling. A normal 404 or connection failure for an archived permalink raises from open-uri and aborts the entire import, even though that thread's comments and all subsequent threads are already available in the XML export. Retain a permalink-only fallback when retrieving the source article fails so the comment migration can still complete.

Update dependency locks for the other supported Rails boot modes

The new dependencies are unconditional, but only Gemfile_rails4.lock is updated. This Gemfile still selects Gemfile.lock in RAILS3 mode and Gemfile_rails_master.lock in RAILS_MASTER mode. Frozen or deployment installs using those modes now have lockfiles that disagree with the Gemfile and fail dependency installation. Update the corresponding lockfiles or scope the dependencies to the supported mode.

false_positives.candidate:
Do not change notification preferences through an unprotected GET

This GET invokes TopicsController#unsubscribe, which immediately saves a new notification level for the logged-in user. The URL is predictable, has no unsubscribe token, and bypasses check_xhr; Rails' normal CSRF protection does not validate GET requests. An attacker can therefore send a logged-in victim through a cross-site navigation to silence notifications for an accessible topic. Make GET display a confirmation and perform the change through a CSRF-protected POST.

Persist the unsubscribe change during client-side navigation

This route only loads the ordinary topic view; it never invokes the unsubscribe endpoint or changes the notification level. If an already-loaded Discourse application navigates to the unsubscribe URL client-side, the initial HTML request to TopicsController#unsubscribe never happens. The page nevertheless tells the user notifications will stop, while their subscription remains unchanged. The client-side flow needs to perform the subscription change explicitly.

Mark unsubscription as an explicit notification preference change

Saving notification_level directly bypasses the bookkeeping in TopicUser.change, particularly setting notifications_reason_id to user_changed. For an existing topic-user row whose reason is NULL, an unsubscribe can set the level to Muted but leave it eligible for automatic tracking. TopicUser.update_last_read then changes it back to Tracking once the reading-time threshold is met, undoing the mute and re-enabling notifications. Use the normal notification-change helper so the explicit preference is preserved.

Keep the topic URL optional in the shared unsubscribe footer

The shared unsubscribe_link translation now unconditionally requires unsubscribe_url, but Email::MessageBuilder still accepts add_unsubscribe_link without supplying that value. A previously supported call such as MessageBuilder.new(address, body: "hello", add_unsubscribe_link: true).body now raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument instead of building an email. Both text and HTML footer generation use this translation. Preserve the generic preferences-only footer and add the topic paragraph only when a topic unsubscribe URL is available.

Do not promise that Regular disables all topic notifications

The confirmation says the user will stop receiving notifications for the topic, but the controller changes Watching or Tracking users to Regular rather than Muted. Regular still allows notifications and notification emails for mentions and replies to the user, so the confirmation promises more than the operation provides. Describe the notifications that remain enabled, or change the operation to match the promise.

On GNU sed, used on Linux, it is interpreted as an empty editing script and the substitution expression is treated as a filename, so an existing GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is not replaced. The script still prints that the update succeeded, leaving webhook subscriptions pointed at the old tunnel. Use a portable replacement mechanism or handle BSD and GNU sed separately.

false_positives.candidate:
Invalidate connected calendars after deleting the cache

The delete-cache success handler only invokes an optional onSuccess callback; it never invalidates the connectedCalendars query. The wrapper forwards props.onChanged rather than refetching its query, and disables refetchOnWindowFocus. When no callback is supplied, deletion succeeds but the UI continues showing the deleted cache's timestamp and deletion action until a reload. Invalidate connectedCalendars here, as the disconnect mutation already does.

Resolve backing cache records for in-memory delegated connections

An in-memory delegated Google connection has a synthetic negative credential ID, but CalendarCacheRepository.getCachedAvailability can serve it from a real credential's cache using userId and the calendar key. Looking up status only by the synthetic ID always returns null. The connected-calendar helper also hides the matching nondelegated connection, so delegated users cannot inspect or clear cache that is actually serving their availability. Resolve the backing user-owned cache for these connections; the deletion handler must likewise support that ownership resolution rather than requiring the synthetic ID to exist in Credential.

Resolve the environment file relative to the script location

ENV_FILE is resolved relative to the caller's working directory. Running bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repository root therefore writes ../.env outside the repository, creating it if necessary, instead of updating the repository's environment file. true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Check the actual slot end against working hours

`end` is calculated from `slotStartTime` again, so the event duration is ignored. With a fixed host available 09:00–10:00 UTC, a rotating host's override can generate a 60-minute 09:30–10:30 candidate that passes this check as if it ended at 09:30. This still offers round-robin events extending beyond the fixed host's availability.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the exact same bug: the `end` time is erroneously calculated using `slotStartTime` instead of the actual slot end time (`slotEndTime`).

false_positives.candidate:
Date overrides bypass booking and calendar conflict checks

When an override applies, this branch returns true before checking `busy`. A user with a 10:00–11:00 override and an existing 10:00–10:30 booking or calendar event will therefore have the occupied 10:00 slot advertised as available. Both fixed and rotating hosts pass their overrides into this function. Overrides should replace working hours, not bypass busy-time checks.

Require the entire slot to fit inside the override

These checks reject only completely disjoint intervals, so partial overlap is treated as availability. For example, a fixed host's 10:00–11:00 override accepts a 09:30–10:30 candidate generated by a rotating host, even though the fixed host is unavailable for the first half-hour. Check that the slot starts at or after the override start and ends at or before its end.

Treat working-hour windows as alternatives

The `find` rejects a slot if any working-hour window excludes it. For a schedule with 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00 on the same weekday, morning slots are rejected by the afternoon window and afternoon slots by the morning window, leaving no availability. A slot should be accepted when it fits one applicable window, not required to fit every window.

Do not reject valid slots against another override window

A date can contain multiple override intervals, but this search rejects a slot whenever it is disjoint from any interval on that date. With 10:00–11:00 and 14:00–15:00 UTC overrides, the valid 10:00 slot is rejected by the second interval and the valid 14:00 slot by the first. Consequently, split date overrides lose all their slots, including on personal events.

Split timezone-converted overrides across attendee dates

Keeping only the converted hour and minute discards date rollover. A 10:00–12:00 UTC override viewed in Pacific/Tongatapu (UTC+13) becomes 23:00–01:00, represented here as startTime 1380 and endTime 60. `buildSlots` skips that range because its start exceeds its end, so the availability disappears instead of being split across two attendee dates.

Avoid applying DST compensation twice to overrides

These offsets use the override date, but `buildSlots` subsequently applies `organizerDSTDiff - inviteeDSTDiff` based on today's offsets. If New York is currently UTC−5 and a future 10:00–11:00 override occurs while it is UTC−4, a UTC attendee's slot is correctly converted to 14:00 here, then shifted back to 13:00 by `buildSlots` and rejected by the availability check. Already date-adjusted overrides must not receive that second DST correction.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

Both failure paths assign reminder.retryCount + 1 using the value fetched before processing the batch. If two cron invocations load retryCount = 0 and both fail, both write 1, so two failed attempts are recorded as only one and the reminder is attempted again instead of being retired. Repeated overlaps similarly undercount failures. Use Prisma's atomic increment operation in both failure paths so concurrent failures are not lost.

Both recommend using Prisma's atomic increment operation in both failure paths.

false_positives.candidate:
Exclude successfully scheduled reminders from retry cleanup

The retry-count branch deletes reminders regardless of their scheduled status. If overlapping cron invocations load an unscheduled reminder with retryCount = 1, one can successfully store scheduled = true and the Twilio reference while the other fails and writes retryCount = 2. The next invocation then deletes the successfully scheduled reminder even though its send date is still in the future. Twilio's message remains queued, but its reference is lost, preventing subsequent cancellation or rescheduling. Restrict exhausted-retry cleanup to reminders that are still unscheduled.

Keep failure bookkeeping from escaping the per-reminder catch

If another cron invocation's cleanup deletes a reminder after this invocation loads its batch, updating that reminder raises Prisma's record-not-found error. The catch now attempts another update against the same deleted ID, and that rejection is unhandled. Consequently, one stale reminder aborts the entire request and leaves all later reminders unprocessed, whereas the previous catch logged the error and continued. Handle missing rows or separately guard the retry-count write so it cannot terminate the batch.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

Previously that preserved the current refresh token; now the literal string 'refresh_token' overwrites it. The next native refresh submits that placeholder and fails, requiring the user to reconnect. Leave an omitted refresh token absent so callers can retain the existing value.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

Zoom then calculates its expiry from undefined, while Office365 retains an already-expired value. Preserve and validate the actual response fields.

While they slightly differ in describing the exact runtime behavior (throwing an error vs evaluating to '[object Object]' and stripping fields), they point to the exact same flawed code pattern and underlying issue.

true_positives.matched_candidate:

Saving that result as credential.key moves all OAuth fields under data. The next GoogleCalendarService instance cannot read the stored access token, refresh token, or expiry at their expected locations, breaking the integration after a successful refresh even when credential sharing is disabled.

true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. Consequently, even a successful JSON response from the sync endpoint causes exceptions or undefined token values for these integrations. Decode and normalize the remote response, and adapt the callers to a consistent result contract.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The third argument to refreshOAuthTokens is serialized as calcomUserId, but this call passes credentialId. Credential IDs and user IDs identify different records, so the external store can either fail the lookup or return another user's OAuth token, which is then saved on this credential. true_positives.golden_comment: The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Use the refreshed Salesforce token for the current connection

The new refresh result is written to the database but never applied to credentialKey. The jsforce.Connection constructed immediately afterward still receives the original access_token and instance_url. If the original token is expired, the current operation uses that expired token and jsforce must refresh again despite the successful refresh just performed. Initialize the connection from the refreshed values instead of adding a redundant token request and database write.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the exact same bug: after a token refresh, the newly created `jsforce.Connection` still uses the stale `access_token` and `instance_url` from `credentialKey` instead of the newly refreshed values.

false_positives.candidate:
Import Prisma before using the new credential update

The new code calls prisma.credential.update, but this module neither imports nor declares prisma. This fails TypeScript checking and, in builds that skip type checking, throws a ReferenceError whenever Salesforce client initialization reaches the database update.

Authenticate outbound credential-refresh requests

The request to the external token broker contains only a guessable calcomUserId and appSlug, with no authentication header or other caller credential. For an Internet-reachable sync endpoint, requests generated by this protocol are indistinguishable from requests made by an attacker seeking another user's access token. An endpoint enforcing shared-secret authentication would instead reject every refresh. Add an authenticated exchange, such as sending the configured shared secret in the configured header.

Use the canonical Zoom app slug in sync requests

This sends appSlug='zoomvideo', but Zoom credentials are created with appId='zoom' and its app keys are also looked up using 'zoom'. 'zoomvideo' is the integration directory name, not the app-store slug used by the new webhook contract. An external store indexing credentials by the canonical app slug cannot resolve this request, so Zoom token synchronization fails.

Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured sync endpoint

The newly added refresh always posts directly to Salesforce and never uses refreshOAuthTokens. Even when credential sharing and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are configured, Salesforce therefore ignores the platform designated as the credential source of truth and still requires a usable local refresh token. Platform-managed credentials cannot follow the new refresh flow. Apply the same user/team-aware sync routing used by the other adapters.

The shared helper documents a sync response containing only an access token and expiry, but Webex still validates it with webexRefreshedTokenSchema, which requires scope, token_type, refresh_token, and refresh_token_expires_in. A compliant sync response is therefore rejected before its token is used, breaking Webex operations once the old token expires. Lark has the same mismatch: it expects nested data.data and refresh-token metadata. These adapters need sync-specific response handling rather than retaining native OAuth response requirements.

Make webhook credential creation idempotent under concurrent delivery

Finding an existing credential and creating one are separate, unsynchronized operations. Two concurrent first deliveries for the same user and app can both observe no credential and create separate rows. Subsequent deliveries update only one row through findFirst, leaving another installed credential with stale tokens. Serialize the keyed find-or-create operation or use an appropriate uniqueness and retry mechanism so concurrent webhook delivery cannot create duplicate credentials.

Clear the invalid flag when replacing invalid credentials

Google, Zoom, and Webex mark credential rows invalid=true after an invalid_grant. When the source platform reconnects an account and sends working replacement keys, this webhook finds the existing row and changes only key, leaving invalid=true. The refreshed integration remains marked invalid despite the successful sync response and cannot be restored through this endpoint without deleting or reinstalling it. Reset the invalid state when accepting replacement credentials.

This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

Await reminder cancellation persistence before completing the request

The asynchronous cancellation helpers are called from forEach without awaiting or collecting their promises, and they are absent from the subsequent Promise.all. These helpers now perform the only database update or deletion that prevents the cron from sending a cancelled booking's reminders. The handler can return while those writes are pending; in a serverless deployment, execution may be suspended before they finish, leaving live reminders behind despite a successful cancellation response. Include these promises in the awaited work.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the same bug: asynchronous reminder cancellation functions (deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder) are called inside a forEach loop without awaiting their promises, which can cause reminders to remain active instead of being reliably cancelled.

false_positives.candidate:

If a booking is cancelled just after a cron run and its reminder is due 12 minutes later, SendGrid sends the reminder before the next run. That run then deletes the now-past reminder row before processing cancellations. Near-due reminders need synchronous cancellation; otherwise cancelled bookings still receive reminders even when the cron runs reliably.

Passing true makes deleteScheduledEmailReminder cancel immediately even when the original reminder is scheduled days away. Those cancellations occupy SendGrid's 100 pending-cancellation slots until their original send dates, recreating the quota exhaustion described in this PR. Once the quota is full, the helper only logs the failure and never marks the reminder cancelled, so the cron cannot retry it and the old reminder is sent. The try/catch surrounds the entire cancellation loop, so one rejected SendGrid request skips every remaining reminder and also skips Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete). Because Prisma queries are lazy, even the database deletions queued for earlier successful cancellations never execute. A persistently failing batch can therefore block other cancellations across cron runs until reminders are sent or removed as past. Catch failures per reminder and execute each successful cancellation's deletion independently.

The Lost access control exists only in TwoFactorFooter, while Google/SAML 2FA redirects set totpEmail and render ExternalTotpFooter, which offers only Cancel. Use datetime cursor conversion for the audit-log paginator

The audit-log endpoint selects this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, but `get_item_key` calls math.floor/math.ceil on the resulting datetime object. false_positives.candidate:
Migrate existing Redis sets before switching to sorted sets

The previous implementation stores ordinary Redis sets under the same `span-buf:s:*` keys now used by ZADD, ZSCAN, and the Lua sorted-set commands. Existing buffered segments therefore cause WRONGTYPE errors during insertion and flushing after deployment. No conversion, drain, or versioned namespace is provided, so affected processing can remain blocked until those keys expire. Introduce a compatible migration or a new key namespace before changing the Redis data type.

Preserve timestamp scores when merging overlapping buffers

Both ZUNIONSTORE calls use Redis's default SUM aggregation. If a child span is replayed after its parent buffer has been redirected, its payload can exist in both the temporary parent buffer and the destination buffer. Merging then doubles its end-timestamp score instead of preserving it. The subsequent ZPOPMIN eviction treats that old replayed span as newer than genuinely recent spans and discards the wrong data. Specify an aggregation such as MAX to keep merges idempotent for overlapping payloads.

Honor the configured maximum segment span count

Removing the span-count check leaves `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` unused, while the Lua script always trims to 1000 spans. Callers configuring a smaller maximum now receive segments exceeding that limit, and callers configuring a larger maximum silently lose spans at 1000. Pass the configured limit into the insertion script and use it for eviction rather than retaining a constructor option that no longer controls the buffer.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Accessing .has_global_access on organization_context.member can raise an AttributeError when organization_context is None, particularly for non-superuser non-member users.

true_positives.golden_comment: The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Check the dataset actually used for split dashboard queries

The eligibility check receives the enclosing request's dataset rather than scoped_dataset. For a metrics-enhanced dashboard request whose widget is split to ERROR_EVENTS, get_event_stats_factory explicitly executes the query against Discover, but this check still sees the metrics dataset and always rejects upsampling. Even with allowlisted projects and an explicit event.type:error filter, that error chart returns raw sampled counts. Base eligibility on the dataset and effective query actually being executed.
true_positives.reasoning: Both say the eligibility check uses the outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset. Both note that for a dashboard split to discover with metrics as the original dataset, upsampling gets skipped despite allowlisted projects.

false_positives.candidate:
Require an error-only filter instead of a substring match

The substring check also accepts queries such as `!event.type:error` and `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`. For allowlisted projects, these queries consequently have count() replaced with the error-only sample_weight aggregation even though they can select transactions, where sample_weight is unsupported. This can break valid Discover queries or return incorrect counts. Eligibility needs to establish from the parsed filter that every matching event is an error, accounting for negation and OR branches.

Apply upsampling to top-N selection, not just its time series

Only timeseries_columns are transformed; selected_columns and orderby still contain the original count() aggregation. A request grouping by issue and ordering by descending count therefore selects top issues by ingested event count but displays their upsampled counts. With varying sampling rates, an issue containing one event of weight 10 can be excluded in favor of an issue containing two events of weight 1. Transform the aggregation used for top-N selection as well so selection and displayed counts use the same measure.

Verify counting of unsampled historical errors

Both fixture events have client_sample_rate=0.1, so the tests only verify rows with explicit sampling metadata. Allowlisting a project also affects queries over its pre-rollout errors, which lack that metadata. The new aggregation directly sums sample_weight and relies on a schema-default assumption that these tests never verify. Add an allowlisted-project test with unsampled errors, including a mixture of sampled and unsampled rows, and assert that each unsampled error still contributes one to the count.

Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.

true_positives.golden_comment: The cache key construction in `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses simple string concatenation with underscores, which can lead to ambiguous keys and collision risks when any component contains underscores or is empty. Joining the resource name and parent folder with underscores creates collisions for UIDs containing underscores. For example, `(name="a_b", parent="c")` and `(name="a", parent="b_c")` produce the same key for the same user and action. Denying the first request therefore also denies the second, even if its permissions allow access, because denial-cache hits bypass permission evaluation. Use an escaped, length-prefixed, or structured encoding of the components.

The denial key uses only the parsed UserUID, so distinct subjects such as `anonymous:0` and `render:0` share an entry for the same action, resource name, and folder. If an anonymous dashboard-read check is denied, a subsequent renderer check hits that denial before reaching the renderer's unconditional read grant. This incorrectly blocks rendering for 30 seconds. Include the identity type or full typed subject in the key.

false_positives.candidate:
Fail closed when the installation has no local Integration row

The Integration.DoesNotExist branch advances without comparing the OAuth user to the installation's sender. GitHub installation webhooks are asynchronous and can fail, so a valid installation can exist on GitHub without a local Integration row. An attacker authenticated with their own GitHub account can supply that installation ID and reach build_integration, which uses app credentials to fetch and attach it to the attacker's Sentry organization. Obtain trusted authorization data or reject the request when the local verification data is unavailable instead of skipping verification.

Compare immutable GitHub user IDs instead of logins

The authenticated identity stores only GitHub's login, which is subsequently compared with the login cached in the installation's sender metadata. GitHub usernames can change, and old usernames can be claimed by another account. After an installer renames their account, the legitimate installer fails verification while someone who acquires the former username can pass it and claim an unlinked installation. Store the authenticated user's immutable numeric ID and compare it with sender.id instead.

The GitHub-404 handling in build_integration is unchanged and still raises 'The GitHub installation could not be found.' This test now expects 'Invalid installation request.' instead, so a passing test validates an earlier OAuth rejection rather than the stubbed installation 404. The installation lookup can disappear entirely without this test detecting it. Use the state returned by the authorization redirect, assert that the installation request occurs, and retain the not-found message assertion to preserve coverage of the original error path.

true_positives.golden_comment: Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Register cleanup for the actual provider aliases

The test creates providers named idp-alias-0 through idp-alias-19, but every cleanup callback targets the literal alias "alias". The same mistake occurs for idp-alias-20 at line 425. These callbacks never remove the created providers and can receive 404 responses during cleanup, leaving realm-level providers behind to cause duplicate-alias failures or unexpected login-provider counts in later runs. false_positives.candidate:
Use stored IDP state when deciding login-cache invalidation

The original model comes from getById(), whose organization-aware wrapper reports isEnabled() as false when the organization is disabled. However, the login cache is populated from the JPA delegate using the stored IDP enabled flag. If a cached provider is made hidden, link-only, or non-public while its organization is disabled, both predicates here return false and the cache is not invalidated. getForLogin() then continues returning that provider despite its changed eligibility; when the organization is enabled, the bean's enabled-only recheck can display it. Compare the raw persisted IDP state rather than the wrapper's effective enabled state.

Do not merge query results from an invalidated revision

The query being copied was read before invalidateObject() and getCurrentRevision(), but the replacement is published using the current counter. If an IDP update invalidates the cache after this method reads a query containing organization A's results, a request for an uncached organization B can copy A's stale results into a replacement carrying the newer revision. Subsequent logins for A then use the pre-update provider set, potentially including providers now hidden or non-public. Validate that the original query's revision is still current before merging, or discard its searches after a concurrent invalidation.

Invalidate the by-ID entries populated by login searches on removal

getForLogin() now populates each provider's internal-ID cache through getById(), without populating its alias cache. remove(alias) only invalidates the internal-ID entry when the alias entry exists or is already locally invalidated. Consequently, a login search followed by remove(alias), without an intervening cached alias lookup, leaves the deleted provider's internal-ID entry intact. Later getById() or getByIdOrAlias() calls return the deleted provider instead of null. Removal should invalidate the stored provider's internal ID unconditionally when the provider exists.

true_positives.golden_comment: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Recheck the cache after acquiring the write lock

Concurrent non-development calls to GetWebAssets can all observe a nil cache before the first caller acquires the write lock. Although the first caller then populates the cache, every queued caller still reloads and decodes the manifest while holding the exclusive lock. This serializes redundant initialization work and blocks other cache readers, increasing cold-start request latency with the number of concurrent cache misses. After acquiring the write lock, recheck entryPointAssetsCache and return it when populated, while preserving the reload behavior in development mode.
true_positives.reasoning: Both point to the same flaw: GetWebAssets does not recheck the cache after taking the write lock, so the double-checked locking pattern is incomplete and the work is repeated redundantly.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses Error log level for what appears to be debugging information. This will pollute error logs in production. Consider using Debug or Info level instead.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Do not report successful cleanup batches as errors

The new annotation and tag cleanup paths call log.Error unconditionally after successful queries and deletes. This includes empty batches with no eligible rows and a nil error, so healthy scheduled cleanup now emits error-level messages on every run, often with an entire batch of IDs. This creates false failure signals for operators and error-based monitoring while adding unnecessary log volume. Remove these diagnostics or log them at Debug, reserving Error for actual failures.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments flag the same problem: log.Error is used for non-error, debugging-style messages, which pollutes production error logs. Both recommend switching to Debug or Info level.

true_positives.golden_comment: The cleanup job ticker was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, which can lead to increased database load and contention due to more frequent execution of cleanup tasks. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with performance expectations.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Preserve the cadence of the global cleanup scheduler

This ticker controls all eight cleanup jobs, not just annotation cleanup. Changing it from ten minutes to one minute schedules database and filesystem cleanup ten times as often. The existing cleanup timeout remains nine minutes, so runs lasting longer than one minute can also leave a tick pending and restart immediately, making cleanup effectively continuous. This introduces a broad background-load regression unrelated to splitting the annotation SQL statements; retain the existing interval or schedule annotations separately if a faster cadence is required.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments flag the cleanup ticker being changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, which raises database load and background contention. The candidate adds more detail but describes the same issue.

false_positives.candidate:
Respect parameter limits on PostgreSQL and MySQL

The non-SQLite path creates one bound parameter per ID without capping the batch. PostgreSQL and prepared MySQL statements support at most 65,535 parameters, so a cleanup batch configured above that limit fails whenever enough eligible rows exist. The previous subquery-based DELETE did not have this restriction. Cleanup then returns without deleting the batch and fails again on subsequent runs, preventing retention cleanup from progressing. Cap or subdivide DELETE batches according to the database's parameter limit.

Build the SQLite ID list without repeatedly copying it

Each fmt.Sprintf copies the entire accumulated ID list into a new string, making construction allocate O(n²) bytes. A roughly 32,000-ID batch produces several gigabytes of transient allocations for a final SQL list of only a few hundred kilobytes. This specifically penalizes the large batches the SQLite fallback is intended to support, adding substantial CPU and garbage-collection work to cleanup. Use a strings.Builder or byte buffer to construct the list linearly.

true_positives.golden_comment: In DualWriterMode3's DeleteCollection method, when a storage operation fails, recordStorageDuration is incorrectly called with recordLegacyDuration instead.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Attribute duration metrics to the backend that performed the operation

The unified-storage Create failure is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, although no legacy operation ran. Update has the same mistake at line 129. Conversely, the background legacy DeleteCollection call records recordStorageDuration at line 166. These observations hide unified create/update failures, falsely report legacy failures, and mix legacy collection-delete latency and errors into unified-storage metrics. Use the corresponding backend's recorder at each call site.
true_positives.reasoning: Both flag swapped legacy/storage duration recorders in DualWriterMode3's DeleteCollection. The candidate describes the direction as the reverse (the legacy call records storage duration), but the golden comment's wording is ambiguous. It is likely the same mismatched-recorder bug at the same location.

true_positives.golden_comment: Inconsistency: using name instead of options.Kind for metrics recording differs from other methods.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Do not use resource names as the kind metric label

The successful Delete observation passes name in the argument used for options.Kind everywhere else, including this method's error path. Every deleted resource name therefore creates a distinct duration-metric label value instead of sharing the resource-kind value. Normal resource churn can create unbounded Prometheus series and memory usage, while successful and failed deletions cannot be aggregated under the same kind. Pass options.Kind here.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments flag the same problem: the metric is recorded with name where options.Kind is used everywhere else. The candidate adds detail about cardinality, but the underlying issue is identical.

false_positives.candidate:
Detach background writes from request cancellation

All four background writes derive their timeout context from the original request context. WithTimeoutCause preserves parent cancellation, and an HTTP request's context is canceled when its handler returns. Consequently, returning after the unified-storage write can immediately cancel the legacy write, even though its ten-second timeout has not elapsed. This makes successful requests routinely leave legacy storage unsynchronized. Preserve the request's context values while detaching cancellation, then apply the background timeout.

Replicate the committed update instead of replaying objInfo

The legacy update now receives the original UpdatedObjectInfo instead of a wrapper containing the object committed to unified storage. For PATCH and server-side apply, UpdatedObjectInfo computes the update from the old object supplied by the store. Legacy storage can have a different or stale old object, so replaying the update can preserve stale fields or produce a different result from the successful unified update. Restore replication of the committed result rather than independently evaluating the request against legacy state.

Preserve operation ordering in asynchronous legacy writes

Each write launches an independent goroutine, with no ordering between operations on the same resource. Even a client that waits for a create response before deleting can have the legacy delete run before the pending legacy create. The delete then returns NotFound, its error is ignored, and the late create leaves a legacy object that no longer exists in unified storage. Sequential updates can likewise overwrite newer legacy state with older state. Background replication needs per-resource ordering or an equivalent version-aware mechanism.

Independently verify completion of legacy writes

The new tests give legacy and unified storage the same mock, whose expectations use identical method names. A legacy expectation can therefore satisfy a unified call; the Create error case actually configures only setupLegacyFn yet exercises the unified failure path. The tests also neither await background writes nor assert their call counts, so deleting every legacy-write goroutine would still pass these unit tests. Use separate mocks and synchronize assertions on legacy completion to verify the central mode-3 replication behavior.

Avoid interpolating expanded targets again during execution

true_positives.golden_comment: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.

The optional device header allows clients to bypass the limit

false_positives.candidate:
