The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The new downsize definition replaces the width/height API

Ruby does not overload methods by argument signature, so this second definition replaces the existing downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) method. Calls using four arguments now treat max_height as the options hash and fail when optimize accesses opts[:allow_animation]; calls supplying a fifth options argument fail with ArgumentError. Preserve the previously supported width/height form in a single compatible implementation.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same issue. The second downsize definition overrides the first width/height version, so existing callers that pass separate width and height arguments break.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Do not impose the image input ceiling on attachments

This hard-coded 10 MiB limit applies to attachments as well as images, replacing the configured max_attachment_size_kb limit even though attachments are not downsized. A site configured to permit attachments larger than 10 MiB now has otherwise-valid uploads rejected by the browser before they reach the server. Retain the configured attachment limit and apply the preprocessing ceiling only to images.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments flag the hardcoded 10MB limit for replacing the configured per-type site settings. The candidate focuses on attachments ignoring max_attachment_size_kb, which is part of the golden comment's concern that client-side limits diverge from server settings. It is the same underlying issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Percentage geometry is unsupported by the animated GIF resizer

When allow_animated_thumbnails is enabled and the GIF tempfile has a .gif extension, downsize selects the animated implementation, which emits gifsicle --resize-fit 80%. That option requires width/height geometry rather than a percentage, so all five attempts fail and the oversized animated GIF remains above the upload limit. Use a GIF scaling operation or calculate explicit target dimensions.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same bug: with allow_animated_thumbnails enabled, the animated path passes 80% to gifsicle --resize-fit, which expects WxH geometry, so downsizing fails.

true_positives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Reopen the tempfile after in-place optimization

OptimizedImage.downsize calls ImageOptim.optimize_image!, which can replace the file at its pathname with an optimized file. The already-open tempfile then still references the old inode. Subsequent tempfile.size checks can remain stuck at an earlier size, and the filesize passed to Upload.create_for can differ from the resized file on disk. This can reject an image that was successfully reduced below the limit or record an incorrect filesize. Reopen the resulting file before checking its size and creating the upload, or resize into a separate tempfile.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same problem. In the loop that checks tempfile.size, the size reflects the old file and not the modified one. The golden comment calls this a stale cached size. The candidate traces it to an in-place replacement that leaves the open handle on the old inode. Either way, the loop can keep working from a wrong size and the file ends up handled incorrectly.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Handle an absent TopicUser record

TopicUser.find_by can return nil: for example, a forwarded notification for a public topic can be opened by another logged-in account that has never visited that topic. Access to the topic does not guarantee a topic-user row exists. Dereferencing tu.notification_level then raises NoMethodError and returns a server error instead of unsubscribing. Treat the missing row as the default notification level and create the preference through TopicUser.change.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments say TopicUser.find_by can return nil, so dereferencing tu (tu.notification_level) would crash. They describe the same nil pointer issue.

false_positives.candidate:
Do not change notification preferences through an unprotected GET

This GET invokes TopicsController#unsubscribe, which immediately saves a new notification level for the logged-in user. The URL is predictable, has no unsubscribe token, and bypasses check_xhr; Rails' normal CSRF protection does not validate GET requests. An attacker can therefore send a logged-in victim through a cross-site navigation to silence notifications for an accessible topic. Make GET display a confirmation and perform the change through a CSRF-protected POST.

Persist the unsubscribe change during client-side navigation

This route only loads the ordinary topic view; it never invokes the unsubscribe endpoint or changes the notification level. If an already-loaded Discourse application navigates to the unsubscribe URL client-side, the initial HTML request to TopicsController#unsubscribe never happens. The page nevertheless tells the user notifications will stop, while their subscription remains unchanged. The client-side flow needs to perform the subscription change explicitly.

Mark unsubscription as an explicit notification preference change

Saving notification_level directly bypasses the bookkeeping in TopicUser.change, particularly setting notifications_reason_id to user_changed. For an existing topic-user row whose reason is NULL, an unsubscribe can set the level to Muted but leave it eligible for automatic tracking. TopicUser.update_last_read then changes it back to Tracking once the reading-time threshold is met, undoing the mute and re-enabling notifications. Use the normal notification-change helper so the explicit preference is preserved.

Keep the topic URL optional in the shared unsubscribe footer

The shared unsubscribe_link translation now unconditionally requires unsubscribe_url, but Email::MessageBuilder still accepts add_unsubscribe_link without supplying that value. A previously supported call such as MessageBuilder.new(address, body: "hello", add_unsubscribe_link: true).body now raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument instead of building an email. Both text and HTML footer generation use this translation. Preserve the generic preferences-only footer and add the topic paragraph only when a topic unsubscribe URL is available.

Do not promise that Regular disables all topic notifications

The confirmation says the user will stop receiving notifications for the topic, but the controller changes Watching or Tracking users to Regular rather than Muted. Regular still allows notifications and notification emails for mentions and replies to the user, so the confirmation promises more than the operation provides. Describe the notifications that remain enabled, or change the operation to match the promise.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

true_positives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Explicitly write the selected-calendar refresh timestamp

Passing an empty data object to Prisma updateMany does not advance @updatedAt; Prisma leaves that field unchanged for an empty update. Consequently, this new call does not update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt after a successful availability refresh, despite its stated purpose. Supply an explicit updatedAt value, or remove the call if selected-calendar refresh tracking is no longer needed.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug. An empty data object passed to Prisma updateMany does not trigger @updatedAt, so the selected-calendar timestamp is not refreshed. Both propose setting updatedAt explicitly.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Avoid the macOS-only sed invocation

The separated empty argument in sed -i '' is BSD/macOS syntax. On GNU sed, used on Linux, it is interpreted as an empty editing script and the substitution expression is treated as a filename, so an existing GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is not replaced. The script still prints that the update succeeded, leaving webhook subscriptions pointed at the old tunnel. Use a portable replacement mechanism or handle BSD and GNU sed separately.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments point to the same bug: the sed -i '' syntax works only on BSD/macOS and fails on GNU sed on Linux.

false_positives.candidate:
Invalidate connected calendars after deleting the cache

The delete-cache success handler only invokes an optional onSuccess callback; it never invalidates the connectedCalendars query. The wrapper forwards props.onChanged rather than refetching its query, and disables refetchOnWindowFocus. When no callback is supplied, deletion succeeds but the UI continues showing the deleted cache's timestamp and deletion action until a reload. Invalidate connectedCalendars here, as the disconnect mutation already does.

Resolve backing cache records for in-memory delegated connections

An in-memory delegated Google connection has a synthetic negative credential ID, but CalendarCacheRepository.getCachedAvailability can serve it from a real credential's cache using userId and the calendar key. Looking up status only by the synthetic ID always returns null. The connected-calendar helper also hides the matching nondelegated connection, so delegated users cannot inspect or clear cache that is actually serving their availability. Resolve the backing user-owned cache for these connections; the deletion handler must likewise support that ownership resolution rather than requiring the synthetic ID to exist in Credential.

Resolve the environment file relative to the script location

ENV_FILE is resolved relative to the caller's working directory. Running bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repository root therefore writes ../.env outside the repository, creating it if necessary, instead of updating the repository's environment file. The script reports success while the calendar service retains its previous webhook URL. Derive the environment-file path from the script's directory.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Check the actual slot end against working hours

`end` is calculated from `slotStartTime` again, so the event duration is ignored. With a fixed host available 09:00–10:00 UTC, a rotating host's override can generate a 60-minute 09:30–10:30 candidate that passes this check as if it ended at 09:30. This still offers round-robin events extending beyond the fixed host's availability.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate says the end time is calculated from slotStartTime rather than the slot's actual end, so the duration is ignored. That is the same bug the golden comment describes.

false_positives.candidate:
Date overrides bypass booking and calendar conflict checks

When an override applies, this branch returns true before checking `busy`. A user with a 10:00–11:00 override and an existing 10:00–10:30 booking or calendar event will therefore have the occupied 10:00 slot advertised as available. Both fixed and rotating hosts pass their overrides into this function. Overrides should replace working hours, not bypass busy-time checks.

Require the entire slot to fit inside the override

These checks reject only completely disjoint intervals, so partial overlap is treated as availability. For example, a fixed host's 10:00–11:00 override accepts a 09:30–10:30 candidate generated by a rotating host, even though the fixed host is unavailable for the first half-hour. Check that the slot starts at or after the override start and ends at or before its end.

Treat working-hour windows as alternatives

The `find` rejects a slot if any working-hour window excludes it. For a schedule with 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00 on the same weekday, morning slots are rejected by the afternoon window and afternoon slots by the morning window, leaving no availability. A slot should be accepted when it fits one applicable window, not required to fit every window.

Do not reject valid slots against another override window

A date can contain multiple override intervals, but this search rejects a slot whenever it is disjoint from any interval on that date. With 10:00–11:00 and 14:00–15:00 UTC overrides, the valid 10:00 slot is rejected by the second interval and the valid 14:00 slot by the first. Consequently, split date overrides lose all their slots, including on personal events.

Split timezone-converted overrides across attendee dates

Keeping only the converted hour and minute discards date rollover. A 10:00–12:00 UTC override viewed in Pacific/Tongatapu (UTC+13) becomes 23:00–01:00, represented here as startTime 1380 and endTime 60. `buildSlots` skips that range because its start exceeds its end, so the availability disappears instead of being split across two attendee dates.

Avoid applying DST compensation twice to overrides

These offsets use the override date, but `buildSlots` subsequently applies `organizerDSTDiff - inviteeDSTDiff` based on today's offsets. If New York is currently UTC−5 and a future 10:00–11:00 override occurs while it is UTC−4, a UTC attendee's slot is correctly converted to 14:00 here, then shifted back to 13:00 by `buildSlots` and rejected by the availability check. Already date-adjusted overrides must not receive that second DST correction.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Increment retryCount atomically instead of using the batch snapshot

Both failure paths assign reminder.retryCount + 1 using the value fetched before processing the batch. If two cron invocations load retryCount = 0 and both fail, both write 1, so two failed attempts are recorded as only one and the reminder is attempted again instead of being retired. Repeated overlaps similarly undercount failures. Use Prisma's atomic increment operation in both failure paths so concurrent failures are not lost.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments flag the same bug. Setting retryCount from the stale value (reminder.retryCount + 1) loses increments when updates run concurrently. Both recommend Prisma's atomic increment and say it applies to both failure paths.

false_positives.candidate:
Exclude successfully scheduled reminders from retry cleanup

The retry-count branch deletes reminders regardless of their scheduled status. If overlapping cron invocations load an unscheduled reminder with retryCount = 1, one can successfully store scheduled = true and the Twilio reference while the other fails and writes retryCount = 2. The next invocation then deletes the successfully scheduled reminder even though its send date is still in the future. Twilio's message remains queued, but its reference is lost, preventing subsequent cancellation or rescheduling. Restrict exhausted-retry cleanup to reminders that are still unscheduled.

Keep failure bookkeeping from escaping the per-reminder catch

If another cron invocation's cleanup deletes a reminder after this invocation loads its batch, updating that reminder raises Prisma's record-not-found error. The catch now attempts another update against the same deleted ID, and that rejection is unhandled. Consequently, one stale reminder aborts the entire request and leaves all later reminders unprocessed, whereas the previous catch logged the error and continued. Handle missing rows or separately guard the retry-count write so it cannot terminate the batch.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

true_positives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Do not replace an existing refresh token with a placeholder

This assignment runs even when credential sharing is disabled. Office365's native response schema explicitly permits an omitted refresh_token, and its caller merges the parsed response into the existing credential. Previously that preserved the current refresh token; now the literal string 'refresh_token' overwrites it. The next native refresh submits that placeholder and fails, requiring the user to reconnect. Leave an omitted refresh token absent so callers can retain the existing value.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same bug: a missing refresh_token is replaced with the literal placeholder 'refresh_token', which invalidates the token and makes later refreshes fail.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Use actual field validation instead of computed Zod object keys

Calling toString() on a Zod schema does not create a wildcard property matcher. Both computed keys evaluate to the literal '[object Object]', and the optional definition overwrites the numeric one. Because z.object strips unknown properties by default, a normal synced response loses expires_in, expiry_date, refresh_token, and other metadata. Zoom then calculates its expiry from undefined, while Office365 retains an already-expired value. Preserve and validate the actual response fields.
true_positives.reasoning: Both point to the computed property keys built with z.string().toString() in minimumTokenResponseSchema and call it invalid Zod usage. The golden comment says this throws a runtime error, while the candidate says it silently strips fields. The described consequences differ, but the code issue being flagged is the same.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Persist the parsed Google credentials rather than the SafeParse result

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the complete safeParse result, shaped as { success: true, data: ... }, whereas the previous schema.parse call returned the credential object itself. Saving that result as credential.key moves all OAuth fields under data. The next GoogleCalendarService instance cannot read the stored access token, refresh token, or expiry at their expected locations, breaking the integration after a successful refresh even when credential sharing is disabled.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug. parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse wrapper, and that wrapper gets stored as credential.key instead of the parsed data.

true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Preserve the adapters' refresh-result contracts on the sync path

The sync branch returns a raw fetch Response, but the fallback returns whatever the provider client produces. Google and both Zoho adapters immediately read result.data, while HubSpot reads accessToken and expiresIn directly; none of those properties exists on a fetch Response. Consequently, even a successful JSON response from the sync endpoint causes exceptions or undefined token values for these integrations. Decode and normalize the remote response, and adapt the callers to a consistent result contract.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug. On the sync path the code returns a raw fetch Response, but callers such as Google (res.data) and HubSpot (token fields) expect a provider-specific token object. That mismatch causes runtime errors.

true_positives.golden_comment: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Preserve the adapters' refresh-result contracts on the sync path

The sync branch returns a raw fetch Response, but the fallback returns whatever the provider client produces. Google and both Zoho adapters immediately read result.data, while HubSpot reads accessToken and expiresIn directly; none of those properties exists on a fetch Response. Consequently, even a successful JSON response from the sync endpoint causes exceptions or undefined token values for these integrations. Decode and normalize the remote response, and adapt the callers to a consistent result contract.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments say the sync path returns a raw fetch Response that lacks .data or other expected properties, so callers break. Both also call for a consistent return shape. This is the same issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Send the credential owner's user ID rather than the credential ID

The third argument to refreshOAuthTokens is serialized as calcomUserId, but this call passes credentialId. Credential IDs and user IDs identify different records, so the external store can either fail the lookup or return another user's OAuth token, which is then saved on this credential. Passing a credential ID also bypasses the helper's intended exclusion of team-owned credentials. Thread credential.userId into this call.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments say refreshOAuthTokens is passed credentialId where it should get userId, which causes incorrect user lookups. The candidate explicitly names this same bug.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Use the refreshed Salesforce token for the current connection

The new refresh result is written to the database but never applied to credentialKey. The jsforce.Connection constructed immediately afterward still receives the original access_token and instance_url. If the original token is expired, the current operation uses that expired token and jsforce must refresh again despite the successful refresh just performed. Initialize the connection from the refreshed values instead of adding a redundant token request and database write.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments say the jsforce.Connection is built from the stale access_token and instance_url after a token refresh, and both recommend using the refreshed values instead.

false_positives.candidate:
Import Prisma before using the new credential update

The new code calls prisma.credential.update, but this module neither imports nor declares prisma. This fails TypeScript checking and, in builds that skip type checking, throws a ReferenceError whenever Salesforce client initialization reaches the database update.

Authenticate outbound credential-refresh requests

The request to the external token broker contains only a guessable calcomUserId and appSlug, with no authentication header or other caller credential. For an Internet-reachable sync endpoint, requests generated by this protocol are indistinguishable from requests made by an attacker seeking another user's access token. An endpoint enforcing shared-secret authentication would instead reject every refresh. Add an authenticated exchange, such as sending the configured shared secret in the configured header.

Use the canonical Zoom app slug in sync requests

This sends appSlug='zoomvideo', but Zoom credentials are created with appId='zoom' and its app keys are also looked up using 'zoom'. 'zoomvideo' is the integration directory name, not the app-store slug used by the new webhook contract. An external store indexing credentials by the canonical app slug cannot resolve this request, so Zoom token synchronization fails.

Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured sync endpoint

The newly added refresh always posts directly to Salesforce and never uses refreshOAuthTokens. Even when credential sharing and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are configured, Salesforce therefore ignores the platform designated as the credential source of truth and still requires a usable local refresh token. Platform-managed credentials cannot follow the new refresh flow. Apply the same user/team-aware sync routing used by the other adapters.

Handle the access-token-only sync response in Webex and Lark

The shared helper documents a sync response containing only an access token and expiry, but Webex still validates it with webexRefreshedTokenSchema, which requires scope, token_type, refresh_token, and refresh_token_expires_in. A compliant sync response is therefore rejected before its token is used, breaking Webex operations once the old token expires. Lark has the same mismatch: it expects nested data.data and refresh-token metadata. These adapters need sync-specific response handling rather than retaining native OAuth response requirements.

Make webhook credential creation idempotent under concurrent delivery

Finding an existing credential and creating one are separate, unsynchronized operations. Two concurrent first deliveries for the same user and app can both observe no credential and create separate rows. Subsequent deliveries update only one row through findFirst, leaving another installed credential with stale tokens. Serialize the keyed find-or-create operation or use an appropriate uniqueness and retry mechanism so concurrent webhook delivery cannot create duplicate credentials.

Clear the invalid flag when replacing invalid credentials

Google, Zoom, and Webex mark credential rows invalid=true after an invalid_grant. When the source platform reconnects an account and sends working replacement keys, this webhook finds the existing row and changes only key, leaving invalid=true. The refreshed integration remains marked invalid despite the successful sync response and cannot be restored through this endpoint without deleting or reinstalling it. Reset the invalid state when accepting replacement credentials.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

true_positives.golden_comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Await reminder cancellation persistence before completing the request

The asynchronous cancellation helpers are called from forEach without awaiting or collecting their promises, and they are absent from the subsequent Promise.all. These helpers now perform the only database update or deletion that prevents the cron from sending a cancelled booking's reminders. The handler can return while those writes are pending; in a serverless deployment, execution may be suspended before they finish, leaving live reminders behind despite a successful cancellation response. Include these promises in the awaited work.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same problem: the async reminder deletion helpers are called inside forEach without await, so cancelled reminders may stay active. The candidate covers only the cancellation handler, while the golden also covers rescheduling and workflow updates. It is still the same core bug.

false_positives.candidate:
Cancel near-due reminders without waiting for the cron

Scheduled reminders are now only marked cancelled, leaving SendGrid cancellation to the 15-minute cron. If a booking is cancelled just after a cron run and its reminder is due 12 minutes later, SendGrid sends the reminder before the next run. That run then deletes the now-past reminder row before processing cancellations. Near-due reminders need synchronous cancellation; otherwise cancelled bookings still receive reminders even when the cron runs reliably.

Rescheduling bypasses the deferred cancellation fix

Passing true makes deleteScheduledEmailReminder cancel immediately even when the original reminder is scheduled days away. Those cancellations occupy SendGrid's 100 pending-cancellation slots until their original send dates, recreating the quota exhaustion described in this PR. Once the quota is full, the helper only logs the failure and never marks the reminder cancelled, so the cron cannot retry it and the old reminder is sent. Rescheduling needs a durable deferred cancellation path too.

Handle cancellation failures per reminder

The try/catch surrounds the entire cancellation loop, so one rejected SendGrid request skips every remaining reminder and also skips Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete). Because Prisma queries are lazy, even the database deletions queued for earlier successful cancellations never execute. A persistently failing batch can therefore block other cancellations across cron runs until reminders are sent or removed as past. Catch failures per reminder and execute each successful cancellation's deletion independently.

false_negatives.golden_comment: When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

true_positives.golden_comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Normalize guest addresses before checking the blacklist

BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries are converted to lowercase, but incoming guest addresses are compared without normalization. The server schema accepts uppercase email addresses, so a caller can submit BLOCKED@example.com to bypass a blacklist entry for blocked@example.com and still create and email that guest. Normalize incoming addresses before blacklist comparison and storage.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same flaw. The blacklist entries are lowercased but incoming guest emails are not normalized, so submitting an email with uppercase characters bypasses the BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS check.

Migrate existing Redis sets before switching to sorted sets
