PostCreator.create enqueues feature_topic_users and process_post after its own transaction block, but this caller wraps that block in an outer Topic.transaction. The nested transaction has not committed when those jobs are published, so separate Sidekiq workers can run before the post or topic is visible. If creating the embed subsequently fails, the jobs reference rolled-back records. Job publication needs to occur after the outermost transaction commits.

Handle simultaneous imports of the same URL

The existence lookup occurs before the creation transaction and does not serialize imports. The hourly feed poll and on-demand retrievals can import the same feed concurrently, allowing both callers to observe no embed and create a topic before one loses the unique embed_url insert race. The resulting RecordNotUnique exception aborts that feed's remaining entries, and scheduled polling has retries disabled. Serialize creation per URL or recover from the conflict by loading the winning embed.

Set the retrieval throttle and its expiration atomically

SETNX creates the throttle key without an expiration, and EXPIRE is issued separately. If EXPIRE fails or the worker exits between these commands, the article has not been retrieved but its key remains permanently present. Every later retrieval then reports it as recently retrieved, leaving the embed on the loading page indefinitely. Set the key and its TTL in one atomic operation.

Preserve original thread timestamps during Disqus imports

The old topic creation forwarded the Disqus thread's created_at value, but import_remote receives only its title and creates the initial post with the current time. Replies still retain their historical dates. Imported discussions therefore have a first post newer than their replies and are dated and ordered as newly created discussions rather than preserving the exported history. Forward the thread timestamp through the import helpers.

Do not require archived Disqus source pages to remain reachable

Importing each thread now performs a remote page fetch without exception handling. A normal 404 or connection failure for an archived permalink raises from open-uri and aborts the entire import, even though that thread's comments and all subsequent threads are already available in the XML export. Retain a permalink-only fallback when retrieving the source article fails so the comment migration can still complete.

Update dependency locks for the other supported Rails boot modes

The new dependencies are unconditional, but only Gemfile_rails4.lock is updated. This Gemfile still selects Gemfile.lock in RAILS3 mode and Gemfile_rails_master.lock in RAILS_MASTER mode. Frozen or deployment installs using those modes now have lockfiles that disagree with the Gemfile and fail dependency installation. Update the corresponding lockfiles or scope the dependencies to the supported mode.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The new downsize definition replaces the width/height API

Ruby does not overload methods by argument signature, so this second definition replaces the existing downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) method. Calls using four arguments now treat max_height as the options hash and fail when optimize accesses opts[:allow_animation]; calls supplying a fifth options argument fail with ArgumentError. Preserve the previously supported width/height form in a single compatible implementation.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same bug: the second downsize definition overrides the original width/height signature because Ruby does not support method overloading, breaking existing callers.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Do not impose the image input ceiling on attachments

This hard-coded 10 MiB limit applies to attachments as well as images, replacing the configured max_attachment_size_kb limit even though attachments are not downsized. A site configured to permit attachments larger than 10 MiB now has otherwise-valid uploads rejected by the browser before they reach the server. Retain the configured attachment limit and apply the preprocessing ceiling only to images.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same bug: the hardcoded 10 MiB client-side maxSizeKB overrides configured per-type limits (notably max_attachment_size_kb), causing valid uploads to be rejected before reaching the server.

true_positives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Percentage geometry is unsupported by the animated GIF resizer

When allow_animated_thumbnails is enabled and the GIF tempfile has a .gif extension, downsize selects the animated implementation, which emits gifsicle --resize-fit 80%. That option requires width/height geometry rather than a percentage, so all five attempts fail and the oversized animated GIF remains above the upload limit. Use a GIF scaling operation or calculate explicit target dimensions.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: animated GIF downsizing passes percentage geometry (80%) to gifsicle --resize-fit, which requires explicit WxH dimensions, so resizing fails.

true_positives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Reopen the tempfile after in-place optimization

OptimizedImage.downsize calls ImageOptim.optimize_image!, which can replace the file at its pathname with an optimized file. The already-open tempfile then still references the old inode. Subsequent tempfile.size checks can remain stuck at an earlier size, and the filesize passed to Upload.create_for can differ from the resized file on disk. This can reject an image that was successfully reduced below the limit or record an incorrect filesize. Reopen the resulting file before checking its size and creating the upload, or resize into a separate tempfile.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: after in-place optimization replaces the file, the open tempfile can retain a stale cached size, causing incorrect size checks and file handling. The candidate adds specifics but points to the same root cause.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Handle an absent TopicUser record

TopicUser.find_by can return nil: for example, a forwarded notification for a public topic can be opened by another logged-in account that has never visited that topic. Access to the topic does not guarantee a topic-user row exists. Dereferencing tu.notification_level then raises NoMethodError and returns a server error instead of unsubscribing. Treat the missing row as the default notification level and create the preference through TopicUser.change.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same bug: TopicUser.find_by may return nil, and dereferencing tu.notification_level causes a NoMethodError. The suggested handling is additional detail, not a different issue.

false_positives.candidate:
Do not change notification preferences through an unprotected GET

This GET invokes TopicsController#unsubscribe, which immediately saves a new notification level for the logged-in user. The URL is predictable, has no unsubscribe token, and bypasses check_xhr; Rails' normal CSRF protection does not validate GET requests. An attacker can therefore send a logged-in victim through a cross-site navigation to silence notifications for an accessible topic. Make GET display a confirmation and perform the change through a CSRF-protected POST.

Persist the unsubscribe change during client-side navigation

This route only loads the ordinary topic view; it never invokes the unsubscribe endpoint or changes the notification level. If an already-loaded Discourse application navigates to the unsubscribe URL client-side, the initial HTML request to TopicsController#unsubscribe never happens. The page nevertheless tells the user notifications will stop, while their subscription remains unchanged. The client-side flow needs to perform the subscription change explicitly.

Mark unsubscription as an explicit notification preference change

Saving notification_level directly bypasses the bookkeeping in TopicUser.change, particularly setting notifications_reason_id to user_changed. For an existing topic-user row whose reason is NULL, an unsubscribe can set the level to Muted but leave it eligible for automatic tracking. TopicUser.update_last_read then changes it back to Tracking once the reading-time threshold is met, undoing the mute and re-enabling notifications. Use the normal notification-change helper so the explicit preference is preserved.

Keep the topic URL optional in the shared unsubscribe footer

The shared unsubscribe_link translation now unconditionally requires unsubscribe_url, but Email::MessageBuilder still accepts add_unsubscribe_link without supplying that value. A previously supported call such as MessageBuilder.new(address, body: "hello", add_unsubscribe_link: true).body now raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument instead of building an email. Both text and HTML footer generation use this translation. Preserve the generic preferences-only footer and add the topic paragraph only when a topic unsubscribe URL is available.

Do not promise that Regular disables all topic notifications

The confirmation says the user will stop receiving notifications for the topic, but the controller changes Watching or Tracking users to Regular rather than Muted. Regular still allows notifications and notification emails for mentions and replies to the user, so the confirmation promises more than the operation provides. Describe the notifications that remain enabled, or change the operation to match the promise.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

true_positives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Explicitly write the selected-calendar refresh timestamp

Passing an empty data object to Prisma updateMany does not advance @updatedAt; Prisma leaves that field unchanged for an empty update. Consequently, this new call does not update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt after a successful availability refresh, despite its stated purpose. Supply an explicit updatedAt value, or remove the call if selected-calendar refresh tracking is no longer needed.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same bug: an empty Prisma updateMany data object does not trigger @updatedAt, leaving SelectedCalendar.updatedAt unchanged after a refresh. The candidate's suggested fix of explicitly setting updatedAt matches the golden comment.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Avoid the macOS-only sed invocation

The separated empty argument in sed -i '' is BSD/macOS syntax. On GNU sed, used on Linux, it is interpreted as an empty editing script and the substitution expression is treated as a filename, so an existing GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is not replaced. The script still prints that the update succeeded, leaving webhook subscriptions pointed at the old tunnel. Use a portable replacement mechanism or handle BSD and GNU sed separately.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: the macOS/BSD-specific `sed -i ''` syntax is incompatible with GNU sed on Linux, so the intended substitution fails. The candidate provides additional detail but points to the same underlying issue.

false_positives.candidate:
Invalidate connected calendars after deleting the cache

The delete-cache success handler only invokes an optional onSuccess callback; it never invalidates the connectedCalendars query. The wrapper forwards props.onChanged rather than refetching its query, and disables refetchOnWindowFocus. When no callback is supplied, deletion succeeds but the UI continues showing the deleted cache's timestamp and deletion action until a reload. Invalidate connectedCalendars here, as the disconnect mutation already does.

Resolve backing cache records for in-memory delegated connections

An in-memory delegated Google connection has a synthetic negative credential ID, but CalendarCacheRepository.getCachedAvailability can serve it from a real credential's cache using userId and the calendar key. Looking up status only by the synthetic ID always returns null. The connected-calendar helper also hides the matching nondelegated connection, so delegated users cannot inspect or clear cache that is actually serving their availability. Resolve the backing user-owned cache for these connections; the deletion handler must likewise support that ownership resolution rather than requiring the synthetic ID to exist in Credential.

Resolve the environment file relative to the script location

ENV_FILE is resolved relative to the caller's working directory. Running bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repository root therefore writes ../.env outside the repository, creating it if necessary, instead of updating the repository's environment file. The script reports success while the calendar service retains its previous webhook URL. Derive the environment-file path from the script's directory.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Check the actual slot end against working hours

`end` is calculated from `slotStartTime` again, so the event duration is ignored. With a fixed host available 09:00–10:00 UTC, a rotating host's override can generate a 60-minute 09:30–10:30 candidate that passes this check as if it ended at 09:30. This still offers round-robin events extending beyond the fixed host's availability.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the incorrect end-time calculation using slotStartTime rather than slotEndTime, which ignores event duration and allows slots beyond availability.

false_positives.candidate:
Date overrides bypass booking and calendar conflict checks

When an override applies, this branch returns true before checking `busy`. A user with a 10:00–11:00 override and an existing 10:00–10:30 booking or calendar event will therefore have the occupied 10:00 slot advertised as available. Both fixed and rotating hosts pass their overrides into this function. Overrides should replace working hours, not bypass busy-time checks.

Treat working-hour windows as alternatives

The `find` rejects a slot if any working-hour window excludes it. For a schedule with 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00 on the same weekday, morning slots are rejected by the afternoon window and afternoon slots by the morning window, leaving no availability. A slot should be accepted when it fits one applicable window, not required to fit every window.

Do not reject valid slots against another override window

A date can contain multiple override intervals, but this search rejects a slot whenever it is disjoint from any interval on that date. With 10:00–11:00 and 14:00–15:00 UTC overrides, the valid 10:00 slot is rejected by the second interval and the valid 14:00 slot by the first. Consequently, split date overrides lose all their slots, including on personal events.

Split timezone-converted overrides across attendee dates

Keeping only the converted hour and minute discards date rollover. A 10:00–12:00 UTC override viewed in Pacific/Tongatapu (UTC+13) becomes 23:00–01:00, represented here as startTime 1380 and endTime 60. `buildSlots` skips that range because its start exceeds its end, so the availability disappears instead of being split across two attendee dates.

Avoid applying DST compensation twice to overrides

These offsets use the override date, but `buildSlots` subsequently applies `organizerDSTDiff - inviteeDSTDiff` based on today's offsets. If New York is currently UTC−5 and a future 10:00–11:00 override occurs while it is UTC−4, a UTC attendee's slot is correctly converted to 14:00 here, then shifted back to 13:00 by `buildSlots` and rejected by the availability check. Already date-adjusted overrides must not receive that second DST correction.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Increment retryCount atomically instead of using the batch snapshot

Both failure paths assign reminder.retryCount + 1 using the value fetched before processing the batch. If two cron invocations load retryCount = 0 and both fail, both write 1, so two failed attempts are recorded as only one and the reminder is attempted again instead of being retired. Repeated overlaps similarly undercount failures. Use Prisma's atomic increment operation in both failure paths so concurrent failures are not lost.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same race condition: retryCount is incremented from a stale pre-batch snapshot, so concurrent failures can overwrite each other and undercount attempts. Both recommend Prisma's atomic increment in both failure paths.

false_positives.candidate:
Exclude successfully scheduled reminders from retry cleanup

The retry-count branch deletes reminders regardless of their scheduled status. If overlapping cron invocations load an unscheduled reminder with retryCount = 1, one can successfully store scheduled = true and the Twilio reference while the other fails and writes retryCount = 2. The next invocation then deletes the successfully scheduled reminder even though its send date is still in the future. Twilio's message remains queued, but its reference is lost, preventing subsequent cancellation or rescheduling. Restrict exhausted-retry cleanup to reminders that are still unscheduled.

Keep failure bookkeeping from escaping the per-reminder catch

If another cron invocation's cleanup deletes a reminder after this invocation loads its batch, updating that reminder raises Prisma's record-not-found error. The catch now attempts another update against the same deleted ID, and that rejection is unhandled. Consequently, one stale reminder aborts the entire request and leaves all later reminders unprocessed, whereas the previous catch logged the error and continued. Handle missing rows or separately guard the retry-count write so it cannot terminate the batch.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

true_positives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Do not replace an existing refresh token with a placeholder

This assignment runs even when credential sharing is disabled. Office365's native response schema explicitly permits an omitted refresh_token, and its caller merges the parsed response into the existing credential. Previously that preserved the current refresh token; now the literal string 'refresh_token' overwrites it. The next native refresh submits that placeholder and fails, requiring the user to reconnect. Leave an omitted refresh token absent so callers can retain the existing value.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug in refresh-token parsing: an omitted refresh_token is replaced with the literal string 'refresh_token', overwriting the existing token and causing later refresh/authentication failures. The candidate adds context but points to the same underlying issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Use actual field validation instead of computed Zod object keys

Calling toString() on a Zod schema does not create a wildcard property matcher. Both computed keys evaluate to the literal '[object Object]', and the optional definition overwrites the numeric one. Because z.object strips unknown properties by default, a normal synced response loses expires_in, expiry_date, refresh_token, and other metadata. Zoom then calculates its expiry from undefined, while Office365 retains an already-expired value. Preserve and validate the actual response fields.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same bug in minimumTokenResponseSchema: using computed keys from Zod schema toString() is invalid and does not match response fields. The candidate explains the resulting stripping of token metadata, which is the same underlying issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Persist the parsed Google credentials rather than the SafeParse result

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the complete safeParse result, shaped as { success: true, data: ... }, whereas the previous schema.parse call returned the credential object itself. Saving that result as credential.key moves all OAuth fields under data. The next GoogleCalendarService instance cannot read the stored access token, refresh token, or expiry at their expected locations, breaking the integration after a successful refresh even when credential sharing is disabled.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse wrapper ({success, data, error}), but the code persists that wrapper as credential.key instead of the parsed credential payload, so later token reads fail. The candidate's wording and suggested fix align with the golden comment.

true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Preserve the adapters' refresh-result contracts on the sync path

The sync branch returns a raw fetch Response, but the fallback returns whatever the provider client produces. Google and both Zoho adapters immediately read result.data, while HubSpot reads accessToken and expiresIn directly; none of those properties exists on a fetch Response. Consequently, even a successful JSON response from the sync endpoint causes exceptions or undefined token values for these integrations. Decode and normalize the remote response, and adapt the callers to a consistent result contract.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same bug: the credential-sync path returns a raw fetch Response, while Google/HubSpot (and Zoho) callers expect provider-specific token shapes such as result.data or accessToken/expiresIn, causing runtime failures unless the response is normalized or callers are adapted.

true_positives.golden_comment: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Preserve the adapters' refresh-result contracts on the sync path

The sync branch returns a raw fetch Response, but the fallback returns whatever the provider client produces. Google and both Zoho adapters immediately read result.data, while HubSpot reads accessToken and expiresIn directly; none of those properties exists on a fetch Response. Consequently, even a successful JSON response from the sync endpoint causes exceptions or undefined token values for these integrations. Decode and normalize the remote response, and adapt the callers to a consistent result contract.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: the sync refresh path returns a raw fetch Response, while callers expect a normalized token result (e.g. .data/access_token or accessToken/expiresIn), causing runtime failures or undefined tokens.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Send the credential owner's user ID rather than the credential ID

The third argument to refreshOAuthTokens is serialized as calcomUserId, but this call passes credentialId. Credential IDs and user IDs identify different records, so the external store can either fail the lookup or return another user's OAuth token, which is then saved on this credential. Passing a credential ID also bypasses the helper's intended exclusion of team-owned credentials. Thread credential.userId into this call.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same bug: refreshOAuthTokens is called with credentialId instead of the credential owner's userId, causing incorrect user/credential lookups and sync failures. The candidate adds detail but points to the same underlying issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Use the refreshed Salesforce token for the current connection

The new refresh result is written to the database but never applied to credentialKey. The jsforce.Connection constructed immediately afterward still receives the original access_token and instance_url. If the original token is expired, the current operation uses that expired token and jsforce must refresh again despite the successful refresh just performed. Initialize the connection from the refreshed values instead of adding a redundant token request and database write.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same bug: the jsforce.Connection is initialized with the original credentialKey access_token and instance_url even after a successful token refresh, so the refreshed values are not used. The candidate adds detail about the redundant refresh but points to the same underlying issue and fix.

false_positives.candidate:
Import Prisma before using the new credential update

The new code calls prisma.credential.update, but this module neither imports nor declares prisma. This fails TypeScript checking and, in builds that skip type checking, throws a ReferenceError whenever Salesforce client initialization reaches the database update.

Authenticate outbound credential-refresh requests

The request to the external token broker contains only a guessable calcomUserId and appSlug, with no authentication header or other caller credential. For an Internet-reachable sync endpoint, requests generated by this protocol are indistinguishable from requests made by an attacker seeking another user's access token. An endpoint enforcing shared-secret authentication would instead reject every refresh. Add an authenticated exchange, such as sending the configured shared secret in the configured header.

Use the canonical Zoom app slug in sync requests

This sends appSlug='zoomvideo', but Zoom credentials are created with appId='zoom' and its app keys are also looked up using 'zoom'. 'zoomvideo' is the integration directory name, not the app-store slug used by the new webhook contract. An external store indexing credentials by the canonical app slug cannot resolve this request, so Zoom token synchronization fails.

Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured sync endpoint

The newly added refresh always posts directly to Salesforce and never uses refreshOAuthTokens. Even when credential sharing and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are configured, Salesforce therefore ignores the platform designated as the credential source of truth and still requires a usable local refresh token. Platform-managed credentials cannot follow the new refresh flow. Apply the same user/team-aware sync routing used by the other adapters.

Handle the access-token-only sync response in Webex and Lark

The shared helper documents a sync response containing only an access token and expiry, but Webex still validates it with webexRefreshedTokenSchema, which requires scope, token_type, refresh_token, and refresh_token_expires_in. A compliant sync response is therefore rejected before its token is used, breaking Webex operations once the old token expires. Lark has the same mismatch: it expects nested data.data and refresh-token metadata. These adapters need sync-specific response handling rather than retaining native OAuth response requirements.

Make webhook credential creation idempotent under concurrent delivery

Finding an existing credential and creating one are separate, unsynchronized operations. Two concurrent first deliveries for the same user and app can both observe no credential and create separate rows. Subsequent deliveries update only one row through findFirst, leaving another installed credential with stale tokens. Serialize the keyed find-or-create operation or use an appropriate uniqueness and retry mechanism so concurrent webhook delivery cannot create duplicate credentials.

Clear the invalid flag when replacing invalid credentials

Google, Zoom, and Webex mark credential rows invalid=true after an invalid_grant. When the source platform reconnects an account and sends working replacement keys, this webhook finds the existing row and changes only key, leaving invalid=true. The refreshed integration remains marked invalid despite the successful sync response and cannot be restored through this endpoint without deleting or reinstalling it. Reset the invalid state when accepting replacement credentials.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

true_positives.golden_comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Await reminder cancellation persistence before completing the request

The asynchronous cancellation helpers are called from forEach without awaiting or collecting their promises, and they are absent from the subsequent Promise.all. These helpers now perform the only database update or deletion that prevents the cron from sending a cancelled booking's reminders. The handler can return while those writes are pending; in a serverless deployment, execution may be suspended before they finish, leaving live reminders behind despite a successful cancellation response. Include these promises in the awaited work.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same bug: async reminder-cancellation helpers are invoked inside forEach without awaiting their promises, so cancellation writes may not finish and scheduled reminders can remain active. The candidate adds serverless execution context but points to the same underlying issue.

false_positives.candidate:
Cancel near-due reminders without waiting for the cron

Scheduled reminders are now only marked cancelled, leaving SendGrid cancellation to the 15-minute cron. If a booking is cancelled just after a cron run and its reminder is due 12 minutes later, SendGrid sends the reminder before the next run. That run then deletes the now-past reminder row before processing cancellations. Near-due reminders need synchronous cancellation; otherwise cancelled bookings still receive reminders even when the cron runs reliably.

Rescheduling bypasses the deferred cancellation fix

Passing true makes deleteScheduledEmailReminder cancel immediately even when the original reminder is scheduled days away. Those cancellations occupy SendGrid's 100 pending-cancellation slots until their original send dates, recreating the quota exhaustion described in this PR. Once the quota is full, the helper only logs the failure and never marks the reminder cancelled, so the cron cannot retry it and the old reminder is sent. Rescheduling needs a durable deferred cancellation path too.

Handle cancellation failures per reminder

The try/catch surrounds the entire cancellation loop, so one rejected SendGrid request skips every remaining reminder and also skips Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete). Because Prisma queries are lazy, even the database deletions queued for earlier successful cancellations never execute. A persistently failing batch can therefore block other cancellations across cron runs until reminders are sent or removed as past. Catch failures per reminder and execute each successful cancellation's deletion independently.

false_negatives.golden_comment: When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

true_positives.golden_comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Normalize guest addresses before checking the blacklist

BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries are converted to lowercase, but incoming guest addresses are compared without normalization. The server schema accepts uppercase email addresses, so a caller can submit BLOCKED@example.com to bypass a blacklist entry for blocked@example.com and still create and email that guest. Normalize incoming addresses before blacklist comparison and storage.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same blacklist bypass: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is lowercased, but incoming guest emails are compared without normalization, so uppercase variants evade the check. The candidate's suggested fix aligns with the same root cause.

true_positives.golden_comment: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Accept either the team administrator or owner role

The isTeamAdminOrOwner check joins isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, requiring both checks to succeed. A team administrator without the owner role therefore receives FORBIDDEN when adding guests to another host's team booking, unless they happen to be an attendee. Use || so either authorized team-management role can perform this operation.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same permission-check bug: isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner are combined with &&, incorrectly requiring both roles, when || should allow either an admin or owner.

true_positives.golden_comment: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Enforce guest uniqueness on the server

The uniqueGuests filter only removes addresses already present in the booking; it does not remove duplicates within the submitted array. The server schema also accepts duplicates, so submitting the same new email twice passes both checks and sends both entries to createMany, producing duplicate attendees and notifications. The dialog's Set validation does not protect direct API calls. Deduplicate or reject duplicate addresses on the server before persisting them.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: uniqueGuests only excludes existing/blacklisted attendees and does not deduplicate repeated emails within the submitted input, allowing createMany to persist duplicate attendee rows.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Honor disabled standard-email settings for guest additions

sendAddGuestsEmails unconditionally sends organizer and attendee emails and does not accept event-type metadata. Unlike the neighboring scheduling and location-change paths, it cannot honor disableStandardEmails.all.host or disableStandardEmails.all.attendee. Adding a guest therefore sends standard emails—including scheduled emails to new guests—even when the event owner disabled them in favor of custom notifications. Pass the event metadata from the handler and apply the existing host and attendee email-disable checks.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores EventType disableStandardEmails metadata and therefore sends host/attendee emails even when standard emails are disabled. The candidate adds implementation detail but points to the same underlying issue.

false_positives.candidate:
Use the booking organizer's credentials for calendar updates

The handler allows attendees and team administrators to add guests, but retrieves credentials for the requesting user and constructs EventManager for that user. When someone other than the organizer invokes this mutation, their credentials do not provide access to the organizer's referenced calendar event. Guests are already saved, but the organizer's calendar can remain unchanged or the update can fail. Initialize the calendar update with the booking organizer's credentials instead.

Prevent guest additions from bypassing seated-event reservations

This mutation creates attendee rows without checking seatsPerTimeSlot, remaining capacity, or creating corresponding seat-reference records. The new action is also exposed on seated bookings, and existing attendees are authorized to invoke it. Consequently, an attendee can add arbitrary guests to a fully booked slot, exceeding its configured capacity and bypassing the normal seat-management lifecycle. Either reject seated bookings or add guests through the seat-reservation flow.

Check booking status before issuing confirmed invitations

There is no booking-status validation before adding guests and sending notifications. The UI exposes this action for past PENDING bookings, and cancelled or rejected bookings can also be submitted directly through tRPC. The mutation sends booking-confirmation emails to new guests and CONFIRMED iCalendar requests to existing attendees, incorrectly representing these meetings as confirmed. Restrict the operation to accepted bookings or make its notifications explicitly respect the current booking status.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Consume backup codes atomically

Backup codes are checked against the user snapshot fetched earlier, then the entire array is overwritten using only the user ID. Two concurrent requests can both validate and successfully consume the same supposedly single-use code. Requests consuming different codes can also overwrite each other's changes, restoring a code that was already used. Perform validation and consumption under a database lock or use a conditional update that detects a changed backupCodes value and rejects or retries the stale request.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same race condition: backup codes are validated from a previously fetched snapshot and then overwritten non-atomically, allowing concurrent requests to consume the same single-use code. The candidate adds the related lost-update concern but does not change the core issue.

false_positives.candidate:
Do not let an unverified TOTP value bypass password verification

Password verification above runs only when credentials.totpCode is falsy, but the new backup-code branch takes precedence and never validates totpCode. A request containing an email, a valid backupCode, and any nonempty totpCode therefore authenticates a CAL account without its password. Someone possessing a backup code can bypass the first factor simply by supplying a dummy TOTP value. Enforce password verification for backup-code authentication independently of the supplied totpCode.

Support backup recovery in external-provider 2FA challenges

The Lost access control exists only in TwoFactorFooter, while Google/SAML 2FA redirects set totpEmail and render ExternalTotpFooter, which offers only Cancel. CAL accounts converted to Google/SAML retain their enabled 2FA and generated backup codes, so these users can possess valid recovery codes but have no way to use them after losing their authenticator. A backup-only request would also be rejected by the credentials provider's non-CAL guards, which still require totpCode. Wire backup recovery into both the external challenge UI and its authentication path.

Notify the parent when successful setup is dismissed

After the enable endpoint succeeds, 2FA is already active, but onEnable is now called only by the backup-codes-close button. Dismissing the backup-code dialog through Escape, the backdrop, or its ordinary close control invokes onOpenChange without emitting the successful-enable callback. A caller relying on the documented onEnable callback therefore keeps stale 2FA state even though subsequent logins require it. Ensure every dismissal after successful enablement notifies the parent, or separate the success notification from closing the backup-code screen.

Report clipboard success only after the write completes

navigator.clipboard.writeText returns a promise, but it is ignored and the success toast is shown immediately. If the browser rejects the write, such as when clipboard permission is blocked, the user is told that the backup codes were copied even though the clipboard is unchanged, and the rejection is unhandled. This can cause users to save unrelated clipboard contents instead of their recovery codes. Await the write and display an error rather than a success toast when it fails.

Remove the fixed type from the new PasswordField

The replacement PasswordField still receives type="password". PasswordField sets its visibility-dependent type before spreading the caller's props, so this explicit prop overrides type="text" whenever the visibility toggle is activated. The new Show password control changes its icon and tooltip but never reveals the password. Omit the fixed type when using PasswordField.

Keep the password visibility control keyboard-accessible

Adding tabIndex={-1} removes the shared Show/Hide password button from sequential keyboard navigation. There is no alternative keyboard control for this action, so keyboard-only users can no longer activate password visibility on login and other forms using PasswordField. Keep the button in the tab order or provide an equivalent keyboard-accessible action.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

true_positives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Handle an empty destination list in the Google Meet fallback

When destinationCalendar is null, undefined, or empty, destructuring produces an undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar. Selecting Google Meet then dereferences its integration property and throws instead of falling back to Cal Video as before. This prevents bookings with Google Meet and no destination calendar from completing. Restore the optional access or explicitly handle the missing destination.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same null-reference bug: destructuring a null, undefined, or empty destinationCalendar yields an undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar, whose integration is later dereferenced. The candidate adds the Google Meet fallback context but identifies the same underlying issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Select the current host's destination for non-Google adapters

Each host's credential is passed the complete destinationCalendar array, but Office365, Lark, and BaseCalendarService still select only its first element. Consequently, a second host's request uses the first host's calendar ID with the second host's credentials. Office365 and Lark requests fail for unshared calendars; CalDAV filters out every calendar and reports success without creating anything. Scope the destination to the current host or make all adapters resolve it by credentialId.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same destination-calendar resolution bug: the code fails to select the calendar belonging to the current host/credential and should resolve it by credentialId. The candidate describes the broader adapter behavior, but it points to the same underlying logic error.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Retain organization slugs when team billing is disabled

This reverses the original condition for storing slug. With IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED disabled, organization creation now stores neither slug nor metadata.requestedSlug. The organization therefore cannot be resolved through its requested subdomain, and the slug collision query cannot find it on subsequent creation attempts. Preserve the original billing-disabled condition when rewriting this spread.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same inverted billing condition around organization slug handling: the rewrite causes slug/requestedSlug to be omitted when team billing is disabled, contrary to the original behavior. The candidate emphasizes the disabled-case consequence, while the golden comment also notes both fields are set when enabled, but the underlying bug is the same.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Use each host reference's credential when requesting a reschedule

Collective bookings now contain calendar references belonging to multiple users, but this deletion path still looks up credentials by integration type from the requesting user's credentials. With two hosts using personal Google accounts, both references are deleted using the requesting host's token; deleting the other host's calendar event fails, and Promise.allSettled hides the failure. The booking is cancelled but the co-host's event remains. Resolve each reference by credentialId, including credentials belonging to the other booked hosts.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments concern credential resolution for calendar references in multi-host bookings: the candidate says each reference must be resolved by credentialId rather than using the requesting user's credentials, which is the same root cause as the golden's undefined credential when credentialId is set but the credential isn't found. The failure modes differ (hidden deletion failure vs runtime error in updateEvent), but the underlying bug is the same.

false_positives.candidate:
Preserve credentialId on video booking references

The new conditional discards result.credentialId for every non-calendar result, including dedicated video meetings. handleCancelBooking only calls deleteMeeting when the video reference has a credentialId, so newly created Zoom and other video bookings will be cancelled in Cal.com without deleting their underlying meetings. Keep the video result's credentialId when constructing the reference.

Delete every host's references when cancelling a recurring series

The allRemainingBookings branch ignores the co-host credential fetched by the new outer loop. Instead, it repeatedly iterates the organizer's credentials and selects only the first calendar reference from each occurrence. For a collective recurring series, this deletes the organizer's events repeatedly but never uses the other hosts' credentials or event UIDs. All occurrences are marked cancelled while co-host calendar events remain and continue blocking availability.

Keep co-host destinations when the organizer has no calendar

If neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null. This optional push then does nothing, discarding all connected co-host destinations collected above. A collective event whose first host has no calendar therefore creates no entries for the other hosts, even when their calendars are connected. Initialize an empty array or concatenate the co-host destinations independently of the organizer's destination.

Restore collective destinations during deferred confirmation

Only the first destination is persisted on Booking by handleNewBooking. For a collective booking requiring confirmation, this reconstruction therefore supplies EventManager with only the organizer's destination, and approving the booking never creates the co-host calendar entries added by this PR. Rebuild the destination list from the booked collective hosts when confirming; the deferred payment creation paths have the same singleton reconstruction problem.

Preserve calendar selection for destinations without credentialId

EventManager still supports destinations without a credentialId by selecting credentials according to integration. For those destinations, this lookup cannot match the supplied credential ID, so insertion silently falls back to primary despite a configured destination.externalId. These bookings previously went to the configured calendar and now go to the wrong one. Retain destination selection for this supported credential-less case.

Use a valid Google calendar fallback when the reference ID is absent

When externalCalendarId is null or omitted, the fallback searches for a destination whose externalId equals that same absent value. Valid destination IDs cannot match, so updates receive an undefined calendarId and fail even when the event has a configured destination. deleteEvent repeats this expression and instead tries primary, potentially leaving non-primary events behind while treating 404 as success. This is reachable through references created without externalId and through CalendarManager.deleteEvent, which omits the argument.

Avoid updating non-traditional calendar references twice

The new filter includes references such as closecom_other_calendar, so the main loop now queues updates for them alongside traditional calendar references. The separate non-traditional integration block below still queues those same updates again. A booking connected to both Google and a CRM therefore sends two concurrent CRM updates for each reschedule, location change, or attendee update, unnecessarily consuming API quota. Exclude other_calendar references from one of these paths.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

true_positives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Await the asynchronous reschedule cleanup callbacks

forEach discards the promises returned by the new async callback. Errors from getCalendar, including CalendarService construction failures that previously reached the surrounding try/catch, now become unhandled rejections instead of being logged. Use an awaited Promise.all with map, or an awaited for...of loop. The same regression exists in packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts and the requestReschedule mutation in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx, where initialization errors now also escape the mutation's error handling.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments address the same error-handling regression: async calendar import/initialization failures (getCalendar/CalendarService) are no longer caught by the surrounding try/catch and become unhandled rejections. The candidate correctly identifies the root cause (forEach not awaiting the async callbacks) and the fix (await via Promise.all/map or for...of so errors reach the existing catch), which is the same concern as adding try-catch around the await.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

Await the asynchronous reschedule cleanup callbacks

forEach discards the promises returned by the new async callback. Errors from getCalendar, including CalendarService construction failures that previously reached the surrounding try/catch, now become unhandled rejections instead of being logged. Use an awaited Promise.all with map, or an awaited for...of loop. The same regression exists in packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts and the requestReschedule mutation in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx, where initialization errors now also escape the mutation's error handling.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same core bug: forEach with async callbacks discards returned promises, turning errors into unhandled rejections that escape surrounding try/catch. It recommends the same fixes (awaited Promise.all/map or for...of) and cites the same reschedule cleanup pattern.

false_positives.candidate:
Handle rejections from eagerly started app imports

Every import() here starts when the registry is evaluated, but consumers await only the entry for their selected app. The other import promises have no rejection handlers. If an unused app fails to load or throws during initialization, its rejection bypasses the importing caller's error handling and can terminate the Node worker. Defer imports until requested, or explicitly handle every eagerly started promise.
